# Chapter Sixteen: Scent of the Pack

The fog clinging to the commercial docks of Aberdeen was thick enough to chew.

At 2:40 AM, the rusted, salt-encrusted hull of the Panamanian freighter *Vanguard* groaned against the wooden pilings of Pier 7. A crane operator, heavily bribed through a shell account in Zurich, swung a battered blue shipping container onto the deserted tarmac behind a row of abandoned fish processing warehouses.

The moment the crane cables released with a hollow clang, the heavy steel padlock on the container's rear doors was not picked or unlocked. It was sheared off from the inside with a sickening shriek of tearing metal.

The doors swung open into the misty drizzle.

Eight figures stepped out into the Scottish night. They wore dark waterproof parkas and heavy boots, but none of them moved like mortal men. Their movements were low, silent, and predatory, their shoulders hunched with coiled kinetic tension, their amber eyes cutting through the darkness with predatory clarity.

At their head stood Brock.

The rogue alpha was a towering mountain of muscle, standing six feet four even in human form. His jaw was clenched, his neck thick with knotted cords of tendon, and across his chest beneath his leather jacket ran jagged, half-healed scars from the Rockville garage explosion. In his blood burned an unnatural, feverish heat—the result of experimental alchemical tinctures brewed from stolen silver nitrate and wolfsbane, designed to suppress pain receptors and amplify berserker aggression.

Beside him walked Martin. Thinner, sharper, with slicked-back dark hair and cold, calculating gray eyes, Martin was the architect of the betrayal. While Brock provided the brute force, Martin understood power, politics, and the art of the kill.

"How does it feel, Brock?" Martin whispered, pulling his collar up against the damp chill. "Old Europe. The land where our ancestors ran before the Church drove them across the sea."

Brock inhaled deeply through his flared nostrils, tasting the air. His upper lip curled back, revealing lengthened, razor-sharp canines that glistened with saliva. "It smells like wet wool, coal smoke, and fear. Where is the descendant?"

Martin checked a ruggedized handheld GPS unit linked to an encrypted tracker. "The contact in Rome delivered as promised. The Order transported Victor Vance to an isolated estate outside Dundee—the private sanctuary of Father Edgar MacIntyre. Less than an hour's drive down the A90."

"And the sword?" Brock growled, his fists clenching until his knuckles popped like small-caliber gunshots. "Is Lobera with him?"

"It is," Martin confirmed with a dark grin. "The old priests think they can train an American park ranger to be King Ferdinand reborn. They don't understand that a sword is only as dangerous as the hand that holds it. Vance is soft. He has a wife. He has children. He spent his life writing parking tickets and rescuing lost hikers in the woods. When he sees real wolves, he will freeze."

"He won't have time to freeze," Brock snarled, his voice dropping into a guttural rumble that set the hairs on Martin's arms on end. "He took three of my pack in that house. His little toy dagger burned my chest. I'm going to rip his arms out of their sockets, drink the royal blood straight from his neck, and snap Ferdinand's blade across my knee. When the other packs see Lobera broken, Sowain's peaceful little empire will crumble into dust. The wolves will hunt again."

Martin nodded, motioning toward two nondescript black cargo vans parked in the shadows of the warehouse. "The transport is ready. Let's move before the harbor patrol gets curious."

As the two vans rumbled out of the Aberdeen docks, heading south toward Dundee, another pair of headlights pierced the fog thirty miles to the southwest.

On the private runway of Glasgow's secondary airfield, a sleek Gulfstream IV executive jet sat with its engines whining down into silence. The mobile staircase rolled into position, and three figures descended onto the tarmac.

Alfonso led the way, wrapped in a long dark overcoat that did little to conceal his imposing, broad-shouldered frame. Behind him walked Marcus, carrying a heavy duffel bag containing tactical gear and customized non-lethal ordnance, while Rebecca followed silently, her keen eyes scanning the airfield perimeter.

A black Land Rover Defender sat idling near the hangar, its hazard lights blinking softly. As Alfonso approached, the driver's door opened, and a woman in a heavy tweed coat and leather gloves stepped out.

It was Fiona, an elder of the Scottish highland pack from the Grampian glens.

"Alfonso," Fiona said, her Scottish brogue thick and musical, though her face was etched with deep anxiety. "It has been fifty years since you stood on Scottish soil."

"Too long, old friend," Alfonso replied, clasping her gloved hand with warm respect. "I wish my return were under happier circumstances."

"We received Isabella's message from Virginia," Fiona said, opening the rear door of the Land Rover to let them stow their bags. "Your rogues landed in Aberdeen less than an hour ago. Brock brought seven fighters with him. Our scouts tracked their freighter into harbor."

Rebecca stepped forward, her nose twitching as she caught a faint, lingering trace of ozone on the coastal breeze. "Where are they heading, Fiona?"

"Dundee," Fiona answered grimly, climbing behind the wheel. "Toward the MacIntyre estate. And that's not all. Our hill watchers spotted unusual military activity near Glen Clova. Unmarked black helicopters and heavy transport trucks bearing Vatican diplomatic plates. The Custodes Sanguinis have established a staging perimeter around the ancient abbey ruins."

Marcus cursed under his breath, clicking the safety on his sidearm inside the duffel. "Mercer's death squads. They aren't just hunting Brock. They're setting up a kill zone."

Alfonso climbed into the passenger seat, his expression settling into a mask of cold, resolute determination. "Mercer is using Victor and the sword as bait. He wants Brock to attack the Dundee estate to justify a scorched-earth purge. Once the blood is spilled, Mercer will deploy his weapons against Glen Clova and eradicate every pack in Scotland."

He slammed the car door shut. "Drive, Fiona. We have forty minutes to reach Dundee before Brock tears that house to pieces."
